title: Why I started with messy data
summary: How a pile of confusing numbers made me fall in love with data, and what I’m building because of it.
body:
I did not start with a big plan. I started with a question: how does a pile of numbers turn into a clear answer?

When I joined my BCA at Amity University in Delhi, I picked **Data Analysis** as my intrest mostly out of curiosity. [One line about what pushed you towards it, a class, a video, a moment.]

## The first thing I learned

Real data is messy. Missing values, wrong dates, and the same customer written three different ways. My first big lesson was that the analysis is the easy part. Most of the work is cleaning.

That is why one of my favourite projects is [Dirty Cafe Data Cleaning](https://github.com/Shubhamkeshri433/Dirty-Cafe-Data-Set). It takes messy cafe sales logs and turns them into tables you can actually use.

## Learning the tools

I started with SQL: T-SQL, CTEs, and window functions. Then Python, Pandas, Numpy and Matplotlib then Excel and Power BI. I did not learn them from a list. I learned them by building things and getting stuck and fixing it.

Some things that helped me:

- Pick a small real problem, not a perfect one.
- Write down what broke and why.
- Build it again, a little cleaner.

## What I'm building now

Pipelines, dashboards, and a few AI projects, like an [AI Resume Ranker](https://github.com/Shubhamkeshri433/AI-Resume-Ranker) that compares resumes to a job description using NLP. [One honest sentence about what was hard or surprising.]

## What's next

I want to work on the systems that let a team ask a question and trust the answer. Cleaner data, clearer dashboards, and AI that does real work.

This blog is where I'll share what I learn along the way, including the mistakes. If you work with data too, or want to talk, my email is on the Connect page.

> peace
